name: Belmond Hotel Caruso
positioning: Caruso, A Belmond Hotel, a historic palace-turned-hotel in Ravello on the Amalfi Coast, with sea-facing balconies and gardens
best_for: Travelers who want a historic, sea-view base in Ravello
Guests who like a garden spa and quiet corners

facts.text: The original building dates to the 11th century but did not become a hotel until the late 1800s, when Pantaleone Caruso ran it as a pensione.
The pensione drew Virginia Woolf and other Bloomsbury figures, and later Jackie Kennedy, Humphrey Bogart and Greta Garbo.
Almost all rooms have private terraces or gardens, and original frescoes and vaulted ceilings feature in the rooms.
Balconies overlook the Tyrrhenian Sea, and every room and suite is unique, with historical details.
Villa Margherita is a standalone guesthouse with a private terrace overlooking the sea.
Ristorante Il Pantaleone serves menus by Chef Armando Aristarco, with Bar Caruso for a nightcap.
The Adagio Bar sits among the palace's historic interiors and 18th-century frescoes.
La Piscina is the pool club, where guests enjoy poolside leisure or wellness services.
A massage can be had in a gazebo in the garden.
Ravello is steps away, with restaurants on the square for a drink and ceramics shopping.

highlights.text: The original building dates to the 11th century, and in the late 1800s Pantaleone Caruso ran it as a pensione.
Villa Margherita is a standalone guesthouse with a private terrace overlooking the sea.
A massage can be had in a gazebo in the garden.
The Adagio Bar sits among the palace's historic interiors and 18th-century frescoes.

considerations.text: The hotel is a 1.25-hour drive from Naples Airport.
The hotel is a 1-hour drive from Positano, so it suits a Ravello base more than a walk-to-everything stay.
WhataHotel notes the clifftop location requires walking on steep terrain.
